Optional ARM fast paths with compatibility trade-offs

Routes shader constants through direct GPU memory and removes Funnel diagnostic work from every draw and submit. This can improve performance, but may cause graphics corruption or crashes on some drivers. Restart the game after changing it.

Runs one fragment shader invocation for each 2×2 pixel group. This can strongly reduce GPU load in pixel-heavy scenes, but lowers fine detail and may break some effects. Restart the game after changing it.
Choose the unchanged game setting, force 1× for the lowest sampling cost, or cap at 2× while preserving anisotropic filtering. Restart the game after changing it.
Removes GPU buffer and image bounds protection. This may speed up shader-heavy games, but invalid accesses can corrupt graphics or crash the driver. Restart the game after changing it.
Profiles hot guest control-flow edges while preserving the current JIT as the baseline and immediate fallback. Restart the game after changing it.
Compiles stable hot direct paths as optimized Tier 2 traces. Requires Tiered JIT; unsafe or changed paths remain on the baseline JIT. Restart the game after changing it.

Experimental: uses direct ARM loads and stores only for direct stack-relative accesses while keeping all other guest memory operations strict. Disabled by default until escaped stack addresses can be proven private. Restart the game after changing it.
Uses one ARM64 FMADD for proven scalar MUL+ADD chains. This removes an intermediate rounding step, so strict x86 floating-point results remain the default. Restart the game after changing it.

On Android 12 and newer, groups Game:Main, GpuComm, FMOD and worker threads into a frame workload and reports actual frame time against the 30 FPS target. Unsupported systems fall back safely. Sustained performance mode is not used. Restart the game after changing it.
Uses compact ARM flag-conversion instructions when the CPU and kernel expose them. Unsupported devices automatically keep the baseline lowering. Restart the game after changing it.

Uses SVE2 only for profitable wide vector operations and retains the NEON implementation everywhere else. Unsupported devices and insufficient vector lengths automatically use NEON. Restart the game after changing it.
Uses LDAPR only for proven host-side acquire loads. Guest LOCK, fences, sequential consistency, and GPU ordering remain strict. Unsupported devices use LDAR. Restart the game after changing it.
Publishes CPU-side fence labels from one submit snapshot, merges adjacent pages into multi-copy commands, and performs at most one timeline wait for a demand wave. Restart the game after changing it.

Deduplicates pipeline, descriptor, push-constant and dynamic-state bindings; fuses compatible barriers, render scopes, transfers and submits while preserving hazards. Restart the game after changing it.
Uses a bounded background compiler, fast first-use pipelines, safe optimized replacement, persistent driver cache and a negative cache for invalid pipelines. Restart the game after changing it.

Keeps the selected output resolution, adapts effective fragment resolution from 100% to 50% only under GPU pressure, enables FSR for genuine upscales, and manages texture residency from the device memory budget. Restart the game after changing it.
Uses ARM NEON conversion/downmixing, bounded write accounting and low-overhead underrun telemetry without changing guest audio timing. Restart the game after changing it.
